\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- MARM: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.MARM}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- MARM: Results}

\begin{definition}[Memory-machine instructions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MIns}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MIns}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins}
For natural numbers $m,d$ and a set of labels $\Lambda$, memory-machine instructions
have five forms: a register instruction from the register-instruction set; a branch to
one of two labels according to whether the scanned memory bit is $1$; an instruction
that sets the scanned memory bit to $1$ and goes to a label; and instructions that move
the memory head one cell left or right and go to a label.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Memory-addressing program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MARM}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MARM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MIns}
For natural numbers $m,d$ and a set of labels $\Lambda$, a memory-addressing program
assigns to each label an instruction for a machine with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders,
with labels in $\Lambda$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Memory-instruction indicator]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MIns.isMem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MIns.isMem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MIns}
For natural numbers $m,d$, a set of labels $\Lambda$, and a memory-machine instruction,
define its memory indicator to be false if it is a register instruction and true for
each of the other instruction forms.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register-instruction part of a program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM}
Let $A$ be a memory-addressing program and let $\beta$ be a Boolean value. The
register-instruction part assigns to each label its register instruction when $A$
assigns one there; at labels where $A$ assigns any other instruction, it assigns a halt
instruction returning $\beta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic instruction extraction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_det}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_det}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, let $l$ be one of its control states,
and let $i$ be a register instruction. If the instruction of $A$ at $l$ is $i$, then for
either Boolean parameter $\beta$, the deterministic part of $A$ at $l$ is $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Memory instruction extraction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_mem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MIns.isMem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, let $l$ be one of its control states,
and let $\beta$ be a Boolean. If the instruction of $A$ at $l$ is a memory instruction,
then the deterministic part of $A$ at $l$ is the instruction that returns $\beta$ and
halts.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Memory tape and head position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Mem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Mem}
\leanok
For a Turing machine with a memory tape, a memory configuration consists of a
Boolean-valued function on the integer-indexed cells and an integer giving the head
position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machine configuration with memory]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MConf}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MConf}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.Mem}
For a machine with $m$ natural-number registers and control states in a type $\Lambda$,
a configuration consists of an optional control state, a vector of $m$ natural-number
register values, an optional Boolean result, and a memory tape with its head position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One-step machine transition]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
Let $A$ assign an instruction to each control state, let an oracle assign a Boolean
answer to each of $d$ deciders and each bit string, and let $x$ be the input. One
machine step leaves a halted configuration unchanged; otherwise, it executes the
instruction at the current state: a deterministic register instruction updates the
control state, registers, and result according to its register-machine transition, while
a memory read branches according to the bit at the head, a memory write sets that bit to
$1$, and a left or right move shifts the head position by $-1$ or $+1$, respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machine run for a fixed number of steps]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mrun}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mrun}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
Let $A$ be a memory-machine program, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of
$d$ deciders and each bit string, and fix an input bit string $x$. The configuration
after $n$ steps from configuration $c$ is the result of iterating the one-step
transition $n$ times from $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reachability while maintaining an invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.mrun}
Let $A$ be a memory-machine program, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of
$d$ deciders and each bit string, and fix an input bit string $x$. A configuration $a'$
is reachable from $a$ while maintaining a predicate $G$ if there is a natural number $T$
such that the run from $a$ reaches $a'$ after $T$ steps and $G$ holds at every
configuration at times $t<T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Halting with a specified answer]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.mrun}
Let $A$ be a memory-machine program, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of
$d$ deciders and each bit string, and fix an input bit string $x$. The machine halts
with answer $b$ from configuration $a$ while maintaining a predicate $G$ if there is a
natural number $T$ such that after $T$ steps its control state is absent, its stored
result is $b$, and $G$ holds at every configuration at times $t<T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Instruction Step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mstep_det}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mstep_det}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_det, Complexity.LogProg.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, fix an oracle and input, and suppose its
instruction at state $l$ is the deterministic instruction $i$. For any Boolean value
$\beta$, register assignment $v$, optional recorded answer $res$, and memory data $\mu$,
one step of $A$ from the running configuration at $l$ with registers $v$ and answer
$res$ leaves $\mu$ unchanged and agrees with one step of the deterministic program that
keeps $A$'s deterministic instructions and replaces its other instructions by the answer
$\beta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Successor-Time Run Identity]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_succ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{1}
For any memory-augmented register program, oracle, input, configuration $c$, and natural
number $n$, running from $c$ for $n+1$ steps gives the same result as taking one step
from $c$ first and then running for $n$ further steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition of Run Durations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_add}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_add}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.mrun}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, fix an oracle and input, and let $c$ be
any configuration. For all natural numbers $s,t$, running for $s+t$ steps gives the same
configuration as running first for $s$ steps and then for $t$ more steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting configurations remain fixed]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_halted}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_halted}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Fix natural numbers $m,d$, a set of labels $\Lambda$, a memory-augmented register
program with $m$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$, an oracle assigning a Boolean answer
to each of the $d$ deciders on each bit string, and an input bit string $x$. For every
register assignment $v : \{0,\ldots,m-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$, optional Boolean result $r$,
memory tape and head position $\mu$, and number of steps $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a
configuration whose control state is halted, with register assignment $v$, result $r$,
and memory state $\mu$, is unchanged after $n$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Zero-step reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.refl}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.refl}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach}
\difficulty{2}
For any machine with memory, input, configuration predicate $G$, and configuration $a$,
the machine reaches $a$ from itself in zero steps, and the predicate condition on
configurations strictly before the endpoint is satisfied.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transitivity of Reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.trans}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.trans}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a memory-register machine, let an oracle and input be fixed, and let $G$ be a
property of configurations. If $A$ reaches $b$ from $a$ in finitely many steps while $G$
holds at every configuration before $b$, and reaches $c$ from $b$ in finitely many steps
while $G$ holds at every configuration before $c$, then $A$ reaches $c$ from $a$ in
finitely many steps while $G$ holds at every configuration before $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenating a reach and a halting run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.halt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.halt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MHalt, Complexity.LogProg.MReach, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ be a predicate on
configurations. If the machine reaches configuration $b$ from configuration $a$ in
finitely many steps while $G$ holds at every configuration strictly before reaching $b$,
and from $b$ it halts with result $r$ while $G$ holds at every configuration strictly
before halting, then it halts with result $r$ from $a$, with $G$ holding at every
configuration strictly before that halt.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reachability in one step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.single}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.single}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{2}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ be a predicate on
configurations. If $G$ holds at configuration $a$, then the machine reaches the
configuration obtained from $a$ by one step, with $G$ holding at every configuration
strictly before that endpoint.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-Step Reachability Extension]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.step}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach, Complexity.LogProg.MReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.MReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a memory-register machine, let an oracle and input be fixed, and let $G$ be a
property of configurations. If $G$ holds at a configuration $a$ and, starting from the
one-step successor of $a$, the machine reaches $c$ in finitely many steps while
satisfying $G$ at every configuration before reaching $c$, then it also reaches $c$ from
$a$ while satisfying $G$ at every configuration before reaching $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prepending one step to a halting run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.step}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MHalt, Complexity.LogProg.MReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.MReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ be a predicate on
configurations. If $G$ holds at a configuration $a$ and the configuration after one step
from $a$ halts with result $r$, with $G$ holding at every configuration strictly before
that halt, then $a$ itself halts with result $r$, with $G$ holding at every
configuration strictly before that halt.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Immediate return halts]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.ret}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.ret}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt, Complexity.LogProg.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.mstep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ be a predicate on
machine configurations. If the instruction at control state $l$ is a deterministic
return of the Boolean value $r$, and $G$ holds at the configuration with state $l$,
register values $v$, no stored result, and memory $\mu$, then the machine halts on
$x$ with result $r$ from that configuration, with $G$ holding at every configuration
strictly before it halts.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Changing the endpoint of reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.of_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.of_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ be a predicate on
configurations. If the machine reaches $b$ from $a$ in finitely many steps while $G$
holds at every configuration strictly before reaching $b$, and $b=b'$, then it reaches
$b'$ from $a$ with the same invariant condition.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of reachability invariants]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.mono}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MReach}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, and let $G$ and $G'$ be
predicates on configurations. If the machine reaches $b$ from $a$ in finitely many steps
with $G$ holding at every configuration strictly before reaching $b$, and every
configuration satisfying $G$ also satisfies $G'$, then it reaches $b$ from $a$ with $G'$
holding at every configuration strictly before reaching $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of guarded halting]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.mono}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MHalt.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.MHalt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, let $\mathrm{oracle}$ be an oracle, let
$x$ be a bit string, and let $G,G'$ be predicates on configurations. If a configuration
$a$ halts with answer $r$ after some finite number $T$ of steps and satisfies $G$ at
every time strictly before $T$, and every configuration satisfying $G$ also satisfies
$G'$, then $a$ halts with the same answer $r$ while satisfying $G'$ at every time
strictly before halting.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement with the Deterministic Run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_eq_arun}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.mrun_eq_arun}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart_mem, Complexity.LogProg.MIns.isMem, Complexity.LogProg.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.arun, Complexity.LogProg.arun_add, Complexity.LogProg.arun_halted, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.mstep, Complexity.LogProg.mstep_det}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, fix an oracle and input, and let $\beta$
be a Boolean value. For any register-machine configuration $a$, memory tape and head
position $\mu$, and time $T$, if the deterministic run obtained by retaining the
deterministic instructions of $A$ (and replacing its memory instructions by the answer
$\beta$) is still running at time $T$, then at every time $t\le T$ the run of $A$ from
$(a,\mu)$ agrees with that deterministic run and retains the same memory tape and head
position $\mu$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lifting a register-machine run to memory]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.of_areach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MReach.of_areach}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MReach, Complexity.LogProg.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_eq_arun}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, let $\beta$ be a Boolean value,
let $G$ be a predicate on register-machine configurations, and let $\mu$ be a memory
tape and head position. Form a register machine by keeping each deterministic
instruction of $A$ and replacing every other instruction by a return of $\beta$. If this
register machine reaches $a'$ from $a$ in finitely many steps while $G$ holds at every
configuration strictly before reaching $a'$, and the control state of $a'$ is not
halted, then $A$ reaches $(a',\mu)$ from $(a,\mu)$ without changing the memory, with $G$
holding of the register-machine component and the memory remaining equal to $\mu$ at
every configuration strictly before reaching the endpoint.
\end{lemma}
